drhp.business: MRPL's main activity is crude oil refining and manufacturing of petrochemicals, described in the BRSR as "Manufacturing & marketing of petroleum and petrochemicals products" accounting for 100% of turnover. Its principal products are High-Speed Diesel, Motor Spirit, Aviation Turbine Fuel, LPG and Polypropylene, sold to bulk industrial, retail and export customers. Bulk industrial buyers include Oil Marketing Companies, Indian Railways, State Government Undertakings and other PSUs, road contractors and the mining and cement industries, while retail sales run through MRPL and dealer-owned HiQ …

drhp.expansion: MRPL's FY2025-26 expansion was concentrated in downstream marketing infrastructure and in-refinery debottlenecking/technology upgrades rather than a new refinery train. On the marketing side, the Company commissioned 85 HiQ retail outlets during the year, taking the fully operational network to 252 as on 31 March 2026, and entered Andhra Pradesh with its first outlet there — several further HiQ outlets in Andhra Pradesh are at various stages of construction and commissioning. To support the planned retail expansion it upgraded and modernised depot facilities at Hosur (Tamil Nadu), Hindupur …

drhp.one_liner: Mangalore Refinery and Petrochemicals Limited (MRPL) is a Schedule "A" Mini Ratna Central Public Sector Enterprise and a subsidiary of ONGC that refines crude oil and manufactures and markets petroleum and petrochemical products from its Mangaluru complex.

risks.note: Flagged in the BRSR as both risk and opportunity. Key risks are potential operational disruptions from extreme weather events, resource constraints such as water availability, evolving regulatory requirements and significant capital needs associated with energy transition, given the Company's reliance on fossil fuels. Mitigation is through operational resilience measures, regulatory compliance and transition planning, phased investments in energy efficiency and gradual portfolio diversification. Financial implications stated as positive as well as negative.
risks.risk: Climate change adaptation, resilience and transition

risks.note: Non-compliance with GHG emission norms presents legal, financial and reputational risks including exposure to carbon pricing mechanisms, penalties and significant capital requirements for compliance and transition. Rising energy costs and stricter emission standards may also impact operating margins. Addressed through continuous emissions monitoring, energy efficiency initiatives, equipment and process upgrades, best-available technologies and integrating emissions considerations into capital planning.

A material risk given the nature of refinery operations and associated SOx, NOx, particulate matter and VOC emissions. Non-compliance with evolving air quality standards could result in regulatory penalties, operational restrictions or shutdowns, reputational impacts and adverse effects on surrounding communities. Increasingly stringent norms require continuous monitoring, process optimisation and ongoing investment in cleaner fuels and emission-control technologies. Financial implication stated as negative.

Water availability is named as a resource constraint within the climate risk rationale; the BRSR separately identifies water management as an opportunity requiring maximised wastewater recycling, reduced freshwater consumption and advanced water technologies to lower water intensity and strengthen long-term operational resilience.

The Company did not meet SEBI requirements for Board composition due to a shortfall in Independent Directors during FY2025-26; after four Independent Directors including the Independent Woman Director completed tenure on 27/03/2026, the Board and all sub-committees — Audit, Nomination and Remuneration, Stakeholders Relationship, Risk Management and CSR — fell short of composition requirements from 28/03/2026 to 31/03/2026. Appointment of directors is handled by the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, so remediation is outside the Company's direct control. The Secretarial Auditors made an observation on this.
risks.risk: Board composition non-compliance and dependence on the administrative ministry for director appointments

risks.note: The entirety of the Company's turnover comes from one activity — crude oil refining and manufacturing of petrochemicals — with High-Speed Diesel and Motor Spirit the dominant products, leaving earnings fully exposed to refining margins and auto-fuel demand with no diversifying business line.

A significant share of turnover is exported, exposing the Company to global product cracks and trade disruption, while domestically its institutional dominance and its HiQ retail network are concentrated in Karnataka and adjoining southern states served from a single Mangaluru manufacturing site.
risks.risk: Export dependence and geographic concentration of the marketing footprint

risks.note: All refining and petrochemicals manufacturing sits at the Mangaluru complex; the planned Phase-II Refinery M&I shutdown with catalyst replacement in the CHTU unit in May-June 2025 illustrates how maintenance or an unplanned outage at one site directly interrupts throughput and dispatch.
